fields.sample_size: framework built from four focus-group discussions (cesspool entrepreneurs, gulper entrepreneurs, households in Kanyana and Lukuli parishes), six in-depth interviews with business staff and owners and ten key-informant interviews (KCCA, NEMA, NWSC, GIZ, Water for People, entrepreneur associations, Makerere University), observations and a stakeholder validation workshop; eight business models scored (cesspool: mechanised; gulper: semi-mechanised)
fields.effect_measure: scoring scorecard: 15 sub-criteria scored 0, 0.5 or 1 in six criteria (financial 4, institutional and legal, environmental and public health, technological, social, scalability), weighted by sub-criteria count and reported as percentage traffic-light scores (red under 33%, orange 33-67%, green over 67%); no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: Two cesspool models (scheduled desludging and call centre) and three gulper models (mobile transfer stations, scheduled desludging and call centre) scored high for service improvement in informal settlements; for example the cesspool call-centre model scored 3 of 4 financial (75%), 2 institutional and legal (67%), 1.5 environmental and public health (75%), 3 technological (100%), 1.5 social (75%) and 1 scalability (100%), an overall 12 of 15 (80%). Identified challenges: high emptying cost, spillages, access to facilities, high operating costs and stigma. The authors conclude that no one-size-fits-all model exists and that integrating mobile transfer stations, call centres and scheduled desludging would best ensure inclusiveness, affordability and profitability. The institutional and legal criterion is one of six and legal rules are not the exposure.
fields.section: Full text (15 pages, MDPI Water 14:2914): Methodology 2.1-2.3 (data collection, framework, scoring); Results (criteria, scorecards for cesspool and gulper models); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methodology and Figure 1 (scoring); Table 1 (criteria and sub-criteria); Results scorecards; Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods evaluation framework applied to eight fecal-sludge emptying and transport business models in Kampala informal settlements (focus groups, interviews, scoring); read in full text 2026-10-04. Scores are expert scoring, not measured outcomes.

notes: ELIGIBILITY/FIT FLAG: the exposure is service business models and the outcome a scorecard of their potential; the legal or institutional element is one of six criteria and there is no access outcome. Candidate for the criterion 1-2 scope question (like other service-delivery studies).
